title: Postponement of a Set Hearing under Unemployment Insurance Appeals
content:
Postponement of a set hearing under Unemployment Insurance Appeals is governed by the rule below; its first clause has been superseded and is marked.

1. A party may ask to postpone a set hearing. — This clause is **no longer in force** as worded: it is superseded by the current basis on requests to postpone and on requests to hold a set hearing as a video or in-person session.
2. A non-emergency postponement is granted only when it is requested no later than the postponement lead business days before the hearing date.
3. The lead time is counted backward in business days (Monday through Friday excluding state holidays) from the hearing date, so a request received on the last business day of the lead time is in time and a later one is not.
4. A later request is granted only for a documented emergency.
5. A party receives no more postponements on one appeal than the docket's maximum, counted as the postponements granted to that party over the life of the appeal; a request beyond it is denied.
6. A granted postponement resets the hearing within the reschedule window, with a new notice that again meets the notice minimum days.
7. A party who simply does not appear has not been granted a postponement; non-appearance is governed by the rules on dismissal for default and reopening.

## The lead-time condition (clauses 2 to 4)

| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| Event counted from | the hearing date shown on the Department's record of the appeal |
| Length | the docket's postponement request lead, in business days |
| Unit | business days: Monday through Friday, excluding state holidays |
| Direction | backward from the hearing date |
| Comparison | a non-emergency request is in time when it is received no later than the last business day of the lead time |
| Boundary | a request received on that last business day is in time; one received later is not |
| Later request | granted only for a documented emergency |

### Boundary cases (hypothetical hearing dates and a hypothetical lead of three business days; no state holiday in the span)

- *Hearing on Thursday 16 April 2026.* Counting back: Wednesday 15 April is business day 1, Tuesday 14 April day 2, Monday 13 April day 3. A request received Monday 13 April is in time; one received Tuesday 14 April is later than the lead time and is granted only for a documented emergency.
- *Hearing on Tuesday 14 April 2026.* Counting back over the weekend: Monday 13 April is day 1, Friday 10 April day 2, Thursday 9 April day 3. A request received Thursday 9 April is in time; one received Friday 10 April is later than the lead time.

## The per-party maximum (clause 5)

The count is kept per party and per appeal: it is the number of postponements already granted to that party on that appeal over the life of the appeal. A request that would take the party beyond the docket's maximum is denied.

*Illustration (hypothetical maximum of one):* the employer on a claimant's appeal has already received one postponement on that appeal; a second employer request is denied. The claimant, who has received none on that appeal, is not affected by the employer's count.

## The reset (clause 6)

A granted postponement resets the hearing within the docket's reschedule window, counted in calendar days after the postponement is granted, and the new hearing notice again meets the docket's notice minimum days.

## Non-appearance (clause 7)

Not appearing is not a postponement. A party that did not appear holds no granted postponement for that hearing.
